claims.claim: **The commonest cause is a (usually viral) URTI.** Investigations and treatment are rarely needed for well children with a short history.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Young children have 6–12 respiratory infections a year**; most coughs resolve without treatment in 1–3 weeks.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Definitions:** acute = up to 2 weeks; protracted acute = daily for 2–4 weeks; **chronic = daily for more than 4 weeks**. Chronic cough warrants further assessment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Persistent daily cough over 4 weeks: assess and investigate with CXR and spirometry (if able).**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Start with how long the cough has lasted and whether it is dry or wet**, then look for red flags and identify specific causes or recent infection.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Sudden onset without a viral prodrome, or after choking, may mean foreign body inhalation.** Onset in early infancy points to cystic fibrosis, a congenital airway abnormality or aspiration; choking with feeds suggests aspiration.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cough type:** daily wet morning cough → PBB, suppurative lung disease or bronchiectasis; paroxysmal → pertussis or foreign body; staccato in infants → chlamydia; barking → croup; honking, distractible → tic or somatic cough disorder.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **More than 3 episodes of PBB in 12 months warrants referral** or investigation for chronic suppurative lung disease.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine for** infection, work of breathing, hypoxia, stridor, chest signs, faltering growth, cardiac failure, and clubbing or chest wall deformity (suppurative lung disease).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Chronic cough — red flags:** shortness of breath · **haemoptysis** · chest pain · stridor · recurrent pneumonia · recurrent chronic/wet cough · feeding difficulties · neurodevelopmental abnormality · systemic symptoms (weight loss, fever, growth failure) · co-existing chronic disease · abnormal examination, CXR or lung function.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Not recommended: over-the-counter cough medicines and decongestants** — efficacy is unproven and there are potential safety risks.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No empiric antibiotics, steroids, proton pump inhibitors or antihistamines.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Honey has no strong evidence for cough** and carries risks — **infant botulism under 12 months**, dental caries and aspiration.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For every child:** advise avoiding airway irritants (smoking, vaping, wood-fire heaters), explain when to return (transition to chronic cough), and acknowledge parental concerns.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **PBB is the commonest cause of chronic wet cough**: the child is otherwise well, with no alternative cause, and investigations (including CXR apart from perihilar thickening) are normal.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Begin amoxicillin/clavulanic acid for 2 weeks: 22.5 mg/kg bd (amoxicillin component, max 875 mg).**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Penicillin hypersensitivity:** trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 4 mg/kg (trimethoprim component, max 160 mg) bd.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Still wet after 2 weeks: continue the same antibiotic for a further 2 weeks.** Still wet after 4 weeks, or more than 3 PBB episodes a year: investigate as for suppurative lung disease and refer.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Chronic suppurative lung disease / bronchiectasis** (wet cough unresponsive to PBB treatment or recurring off antibiotics): FBE, serum immunoglobulins, CXR, spirometry, sweat test, sputum culture; refer to a paediatric respiratory physician.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Interstitial lung disease:** chronic dry cough with diffuse inspiratory crepitations, tachypnoea, growth failure or hypoxia — refer to a paediatric respiratory physician.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Somatic cough or tic disorder:** honking, disappears asleep or distracted — education and reassurance; consider distraction therapies, psychological support or hypnosis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refer to a paediatric respiratory physician for:** chronic wet cough failing 4 weeks of antibiotics · more than 3 PBB episodes a year · chronic dry cough over 6 months failing treatment (e.g. an asthma trial) · specific cough or red flags.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider discharge when** the child is stable and any investigations and follow-up are arranged.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cough' (Last updated March 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cough/, retrieved 2026-09-23
